content:
Two numeric issues remain despite the earlier rounding-direction corrections being addressed:

1. The reference uses float for the margin and loses precision on a valid input:

1000000
1000000
1

Net result is -1999999, so the exact margin is -199999900%. The reference's single-precision calculation produces -199999904%. Please use adequate precision or exact arithmetic, and add a public/hidden pair with small nonzero revenue and large costs. All 16 currently listed outputs matched my local calculation, so this gap is outside the present suite.

2. "Nearest whole integer" does not specify how exact .5 ties are resolved. With fc=7, vc=0 and revenue=8, the margin is 12.5%; with fc=9, vc=0 and revenue=8, it is -12.5%. Java Math.round, ties-to-even and ties-away-from-zero do not agree on these examples. Please state one rule and cover both signs plus values just below/above a half. This is a new issue, distinct from the non-half rounding cases already discussed by 5DN1L.

Possible close variation: Economic Fun
https://www.codingame.com/contribute/view/115911f1f5b3448f50d3dd6766c6338b1ba349
Both compute profit and profit/revenue as a percentage. Economic Fun derives revenue from units and price, guarantees positive profit and prints two decimals. This task adds loss/break-even/zero-revenue branches and different formatting, so the contracts are not identical. Please compare whether those additions sufficiently distinguish the task.

✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: Nice simple puzzle with clear instructions. Good one for shortest mode.

Goal
* The variable name "Total Cost" is declared before the formulas but isn't used afterwards. "Profit" and "Loss" are referenced in the output requirements but aren't defined. It's inconsistent that the formulas use variable names in some places but not in others. Please rewrite and reformat the relevant sections as follows:

-----
<<Formulas:>>
[[Total Cost]] = Fixed Cost ([[fc]]) + Variable Cost ([[vc]])
[[Net Result]] = [[revenue]] - [[Total Cost]]
[[Profit Margin percentage]] = ([[Net Result]] / [[revenue]]) × {{100}}

Note: If [[revenue]] is {{0}}, [[Profit Margin percentage]] is automatically {{-100%}}.

<<Output Requirements:>>
Your program must output a single line summarising the financial status:

If [[Net Result]] is {{0}}: {{BREAK-EVEN}}
Otherwise: [[status]] {{| Net:}} [[Net Result]] {{| Margin:}} [[Profit Margin percentage]]{{%}}
where [[status]] is either:
{{PROFITABLE}} if [[Net Result]] is greater than {{0}}, or
{{LOSS}} if [[Net Result]] is less than {{0}}.
-----

Constraints
* Please replace all the existing constraints with the following to align more closely with the test cases:

0 ≤ [[fc]], [[vc]], [[revenue]] ≤ 1,000,000

Stub generator
* Line 3: Please change "float" to "int" to match the Input section.

Cases
* Validator 1: Please adjust the case so that the profit margin percentage is an integer and doesn't require rounding.

* Please add Test/Validator 5 where the profit margin percentage is positive and rounds up.

* Please add Test/Validator 6 where the profit margin percentage is positive and rounds down.

* Please add Test/Validator 7 where the profit margin percentage is negative and rounds up.

* Please add Test/Validator 8 where the profit margin percentage is negative and rounds down.

Thanks.
Thank you for the feedback and these are changes I will be making
Once again, thank you for the feedback. I have gone through and updated my clash with these changes and added 4 new test cases. Let me know if you think anything else should be changed!

Thank you for the updates. Two issues remain:

Cases
* These cases don't round in the same direction:
  • Negative & Rounds Up (Test 7): -12.5% -> -12%
  • Validator 7: -64.7674% -> -65%
  Please adjust Test 7 so that both cases demonstrate the same rounding direction.

* Currently 6-digit input values are used in the validators but not in the tests. Please swap Test 8 and Validator 8 to break this convention.

  For future contributions, please also ensure that inputs of similar magnitude are used within the same pair of cases.

Thanks.
Alright, I have fixed these and there should no longer be any issues!
Well, there's still one. I asked you to adjust Test 7, not Validator 7. I'm afraid you have to adjust both now 😉
Oh I see the mistake I made, so now it should be good lol
